parts: Your crypto isn't inside your wallet.
A crypto wallet is more like a keyring.
The coins live on the blockchain. The wallet holds the keys that prove they're yours.
There are two keys. Your public address is like your UPI ID:
share it, and people can pay you.
Your private key is like your PIN and your signature combined.
Most wallets turn that key into twelve or twenty-four simple words,
Guessing a twenty-four word phrase means searching a number with seventy-eight digits.
The catch: there's no forgot-password button.
Lose the words, and the funds are gone. Share them, and so are the funds.
Never type them into a website. Never photograph them.
And never give them to anyone who asks. Real support will never ask.
Whoever holds the keys, holds the coins.
That's why your crypto isn't in your wallet. Your keys are.
